findings.title: Instructional Text Visual Hierarchy
findings.where: Arena and Road, top-center notification box
findings.problem: The gameplay instructions are rendered as a small, thin, white sans-serif font against a translucent gray box that is too small for the container.
findings.why: It lacks visual authority, causing the player to miss vital operational context (like controls) because the eye naturally ignores the top-center area of the screen.
findings.fix: Increase font weight, add a subtle border or accent color (e.g., brand cyan) to the container, and center the text with increased internal padding to create a 'HUD element' feel rather than a 'debug log' feel.

findings.title: Vehicle Silhouette Readability
findings.problem: The car model is a thin, neon-cyan line drawing that lacks depth, volume, or orientation markers on the actual chassis.
findings.why: The player cannot intuitively judge the vehicle's shape or orientation, making armor and weapon placement feel abstract and disconnected from the physical car.
findings.fix: Fill the silhouette with a low-opacity flat base color and add distinct 'hit zone' outlines for the Front, Rear, Left, and Right segments to mirror the armor stats.

findings.title: Interactive Element Indication
findings.problem: The list of vehicle parts and weapon slots looks like a static text document rather than an interactive form.
findings.why: New players will struggle to understand that these lines are clickable or focusable fields, causing friction in the core 'build' loop.
findings.fix: Add a distinct hover-state background highlight and a small chevron icon to the right of editable rows to signal that they are inputs, not just labels.

findings.title: Action-State Visual Contrast
findings.problem: The speedometer uses thin lines and white text that blend into the high-frequency detail of the road/arena textures.
findings.why: Vital feedback regarding speed and damage (the 100% indicator) is hard to read during high-speed movement, leading to 'blind' driving.
findings.fix: Apply a thicker, high-contrast border to the speedometer panel and use a bolder, fixed-width digit font that maintains legibility even when the camera is panning over terrain.

findings.title: Navigational Anchor Confusion
findings.problem: The player's current location is indicated by the vehicle itself, while the 'destination' is an oversized, disconnected cyan arrow floating above the car.
findings.why: The scale of the arrow is jarring compared to the pixel-art/top-down vehicle, creating a visual disconnect that makes the objective feel like a UI overlay rather than a world object.
findings.fix: Replace the floating arrow with a 'pulse' effect or a ground-projected target circle beneath the destination, keeping the UI components smaller and more integrated into the map perspective.
